introduction

1. This memo contains details about the income tax and the Social Security contribution rates for

2026/2027 and the increase in some IS/JSA/ESA/SPC benefit rates from 06.04.26. The rates are
introduced by the Social Security Benefits Uprating Order 2026 (SI 2026/148), the Social Security
(Contributions) (Limits and Thresholds, National Insurance Funds Payments and Extension of Veterans
Relief) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/231) and the Social Security Benefit Uprating Regulations 2026 (SI
2026/218. This memo also contains guidance on the Employment Rights (Increase of Limits) Order 2026
(SI 2026/310) and the Social Security (Contributions)(Re-rating) Consequential Amendment Regulations
2026 (SI 2026/283) which come into effect from 06.04.26.


UPRATING


Benefit rates

2. Any new rates of IS/JSA/ESA/SPC will apply from the first day of the first benefit week which
commences on or after 06.04.26. DMs can find the new rates in the benefit uprating schedule and
benefit desk aids and should bear them in mind when reading examples in the ADM that contain benefit
rates.


Housing costs non-dependant contribution – IS/JSA/ESA/SPC

3. Where a non-dependant lives with the claimant, a contribution may be appropriate. The contribution is

made in the form of a deduction from the allowable housing costs1. (see DMG 23756, DMG 44586 or
DMG 78500 et seq) The new rates of deduction are:

less than £192.00                         £20.40


Not less than £192.00 but less than £279 £46.85


Not less than £279 but less than £365     £64.35


Not less than £365 but less than £485     £105.20


Not less than £485 but less than £605     £119.85


£605 or more                              £131.45

P1011 The main qualifying conditions to PIP are


1. age1 (see P1013) and


2. habitual residency, presence and competency2 (see ADM Chapter C2) and


3. the claimant is not entitled to ADP, CDP or PADP3 and


4. meeting the relevant threshold4 for entitlement under the daily living and/or mobility component
activities and


5. the required period condition5.


Although there is no formal order of consideration of these conditions, if any of the first three are not
satisfied, then the fourth and fifth need not be considered.


                 1 WR Act 12, s 83(1); 2 s 77(3); 3 s 77(4); 4 SS (PIP) Regs, reg 4; 5 SS (PIP) Regs, reg 12 & 13

Total amount of capital
84921 The total amount of capital each person has is the total of the value of each item of actual capital
and notional capital that person has. The total amount of capital of claimants is


1. the total amount of their capital if they do not have a partner or


2. the total amount of their capital and the total amount of their partner’s capital if they have a partner 1.
